name: Jerome Powell
role: Fed Chair — FINAL 2 DAYS (term expires May 15, 2026; returns to Fed Governor seat through Jan 2028; Warsh confirmed Chair May 13)
quote: The tariff effects will include higher inflation and slower growth — significantly larger than anticipated. We are well positioned to wait for greater clarity before adjusting policy. [Harvard, Mar 30 2026]. STATUS May 13 — FINAL 2 DAYS: Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Fed Chair today (May 13). Powell's Chair term expires May 15 — he will return to his Governor seat through January 2028. Inflation legacy handed to Warsh: April CPI 3.8% (May 12) + April PPI +6.0% (May 13) — two consecutive days of hot inflation data entering the Warsh era. Final tally: 3 unanimous holds at 3.50-3.75% under the Iran war stagflation shock; Q1 2026 GDP +2.0% (no recession); core PCE 3.2% (above 2% target); CPI 3.8%; PPI 6.0% — inflation problem unsolved at handoff.

name: Christine Lagarde
quote: The volatility we have seen in global markets this week is a direct consequence of trade policy uncertainty. The ECB is monitoring conditions closely. A sharp deterioration in financial conditions or growth could prompt a reassessment of our policy stance. European financial stability remains robust. [Apr 4, 2026]

name: Scott Bessent
role: US Treasury Secretary — Seoul Day 2 Completed (May 13); $30B Managed Trade Framework Set for Trump-Xi Summit May 14-15
quote: The market selloff is an adjustment to a structurally stronger American economy. Short-term volatility is the price of restoring American manufacturing competitiveness and ending decades of unfair trade practices. We are building something durable. [Apr 6, 2026]. STATUS May 13 — SEOUL DAY 2 COMPLETED: Day 1 (May 12): 'very good' — tariff stability maintained. Day 2 (May 13): Xinhua described talks as 'candid, in-depth, constructive.' USTR Greer and Vice Commerce Minister Li Chenggang led Day 2 technical session. $30B-for-$30B reciprocal managed trade framework confirmed as summit deliverable. Critical minerals cooperation deal + Chinese purchase commitments framework also finalized. No formal Seoul agreement signed — deliverables forwarded to Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15). April PPI +6.0% YoY released May 13 — stagflation backdrop for the summit.

name: Kristalina Georgieva
role: Managing Director, IMF (2nd term from Oct 2024)
quote: Our April 2026 WEO confirms global growth at 3.1% in our reference scenario — with an adverse scenario of 2.5% and severe scenario of 2.0% if the conflict continues. Headline inflation has risen to 4.4% globally. The IMF is providing $20-50 billion in emergency support to energy-importing developing economies. We call on all countries to coordinate on debt restructuring, quota reform, and to resist the fragmentation of the global trading system. [IMF Spring Meetings closing, Apr 18 2026]

name: Li Qiang
role: Premier, People's Republic of China (since March 2023)
quote: China's manufacturing PMI returning to expansion in March confirms the resilience of our economy. We are committed to working constructively with the United States on trade, rare earths, and shared economic stability. A stable bilateral relationship benefits all.

name: Kazuo Ueda
role: Governor, Bank of Japan (since April 2023) — Apr 28: Held 0.75% with 3-dissenter hawkish split
quote: We will continue our efforts to achieve the price stability target in a sustainable and stable manner. The timing and pace of adjusting monetary accommodation will depend on economic, price, and financial conditions. [Apr 28 2026 decision: BOJ held at 0.75%, 6-3 vote — three dissenters (Nakagawa, Takata, Tamura) proposed immediate hike to 1.00% — most hawkish internal divide of the Ueda era. FY2026 GDP forecast cut to 0.5% (from 1.0%); core inflation forecast raised to 2.8% (from 1.9%) due to Iran war energy shock. June hike to 1.00% now expected by Goldman Sachs and Nomura barring further Middle East escalation.]

name: Andrew Bailey
role: Governor, Bank of England (term through 2030) — Apr 30: Held 3.75% (8-1), one hawkish dissenter
quote: This is the most difficult combination of economic effects we have faced since I became Governor. Energy prices from the Middle East conflict are very uncertain but likely to have a long-lived effect. In a worst-case scenario, rates could need to return to 5.25% and inflation could spike to 6.2%. Monetary policy cannot influence energy prices — our tools address demand, not supply shocks. [Apr 30 2026 post-decision]. DECISION Apr 30: MPC voted 8-1 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75%. One dissenting member called for immediate +25bp hike to 4.00% — most hawkish single dissent in this cycle. UK CPI 3.3% (March); IMF downgraded UK 2026 growth to 0.8%. Next MPC meeting: June 18, 2026.

name: Ajay Banga
quote: Developing countries are facing a convergence of challenges — high debt, elevated food and energy costs, and now trade disruption. The World Bank stands ready to support resilient and inclusive growth.

name: Pan Gongsheng
role: Governor, People's Bank of China (since July 2023)
quote: The People's Bank of China will strengthen counter-cyclical adjustment, maintain liquidity at reasonably ample levels, and support the real economy. We have ample tools to deal with external shocks.

name: Gita Gopinath
role: First Deputy Managing Director, IMF; former Chief Economist
quote: Trade fragmentation is a significant drag on long-run productivity and growth. Economies that become more closed lose the gains from specialization and economies of scale that have underpinned decades of prosperity.

name: Christopher Waller
role: Federal Reserve Governor; dissented for rate cut at Jan 2026 FOMC
quote: I believe the policy rate is still meaningfully restrictive and that we can gradually lower it. The risks to achieving our dual-mandate goals are more balanced than our current stance reflects.

name: Isabel Schnabel
role: Executive Board Member, ECB (Germany); inflation hawk
quote: We should not be complacent about inflation persistence. While disinflation has made significant progress, wage growth and services inflation require us to remain vigilant. Cutting too aggressively risks undoing years of credibility-building.

name: Donald Trump
role: US President (since Jan 20, 2025); Arrived Beijing May 13 — Trump-Xi Summit Begins May 14
quote: China had their chance to remove the 34% retaliation and they refused. So now it's 104%, effective immediately. They want to fight — fine, we have all the leverage. [Apr 9, 2026]. STATUS May 13 — IN BEIJING: Trump arrived Beijing with CEO delegation May 13; Trump-Xi summit begins May 14-15. Agenda: Iran (ceasefire/Hormuz cooperation), $30B managed trade tariff reduction framework, rare earths/critical minerals deal, Chinese purchase commitments. Seoul Day 2 (Bessent-He): 'candid, in-depth, constructive' — $30B-for-$30B reciprocal tariff cut confirmed as deliverable. April PPI +6.0% YoY (released May 13 — hottest since Dec 2022) complicates the optics of tariff de-escalation as domestic producer inflation hits multi-year highs. Warsh confirmed as Fed Chair May 13; Section 122 cliff July 23 (71 days).

name: Janet Yellen
role: Former US Treasury Secretary (Jan 2021–Jan 2025); Former Fed Chair
quote: We achieved something rare in economic history: bringing inflation down from 40-year highs without triggering a recession. The soft landing was not guaranteed — it required skill, patience, and some good fortune with supply chains.

name: François Villeroy de Galhau
role: Governor, Banque de France; ECB Governing Council dove
quote: The eurozone cannot afford complacency in the face of tariff-driven stagnation. With inflation near target, the ECB must prioritize economic momentum. Europe needs its own fiscal tools to complement monetary easing.

name: Philip Jefferson
quote: Energy prices are a key source of uncertainty in the current inflation outlook. Sustained increases in oil prices could temporarily push up inflation and complicate our path back to the 2% target. We are monitoring developments carefully. [Mar 26, 2026]

name: Austan Goolsbee
role: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago (since Jan 2023)
quote: Stagflation is the worst situation for the central bank because raising rates doesn't solve it, cutting rates doesn't solve it, and staying the same doesn't solve it. The longer this goes where we never got to see the decrease in inflation, that starts pushing rate cuts out of '26 — potentially into 2027. [Semafor World Economy 2026 Conference, Apr 14, 2026]

name: Kevin Warsh
role: Fed Chair CONFIRMED (May 13, 2026) — Assumes Responsibilities May 15 When Powell Term Expires; First FOMC June 9-10
quote: I will not be the President's 'sock puppet.' The Federal Reserve's independence is non-negotiable. The president never asked me to pre-determine, commit, fix, or decide on any interest rate decision. [Senate Banking Committee, Apr 21, 2026]. STATUS May 13 — FED CHAIR CONFIRMED: Senate confirmed Warsh as Federal Reserve Chair on May 13 — completing the two-step confirmation process (Governor vote May 12, Chair vote May 13). Assumes Chair responsibilities May 15 when Powell's term expires. STAGFLATION INHERITANCE: (1) April CPI 3.8% YoY (released May 12); (2) April PPI +6.0% YoY — hottest since Dec 2022 (released May 13); (3) Core PCE 3.2%; (4) CME hike odds ~30% by year-end; (5) S&P 500 ~7,401; (6) Oil Brent ~$105-110 (Hormuz); (7) Section 122 cliff July 23 (71 days). First test: June 9-10 FOMC — hawkish signal, hold, or first hike of the Warsh era?
